f39.summary: Francis Needham, Walsingham's servant with Leicester at the relief of Sluys, reports that they had no intelligence out of the enemy's camp or the town for five days, did not know whether there was any bridge or anything at the channel, and that the channel was closed with hoys and flyboats fastened with chains and strengthened behind with flat boats. The f. 39r and f. 40r cipher words were glossed at the time; the clear text of the letter is not transcribed here.

snip.cap: Harley MS 287 f. 39v: campe nor the towne glossed above its signs, and beneath the bare line whether there was any bridge or not
snip.credit: British Library, Harley MS 287 f. 39v, via DECODE R8479

system: Three-grid pigpen: nine box shapes, plain / dot below / dot inside, alphabet a-i, k-s, t-z in order (u=v, no j); words divided. The Wilkes-Walsingham cipher (key in BL Add MS 5935 per CSP).
